subject: Post-call checkpoints — inference integration & SDK deltas
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@novusai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call checkpoints — inference integration & SDK deltas

Samir / Novus team — thanks again for your time today. Quick written recap + concrete next steps so we have alignment before the pilot kickoff.

What we heard (pain & goals)
- Your primary pain: end-to-end latency and unpredictable token costs when we run candidate generation + rerank for clinical question answering.
- Secondary: outputs must be deterministic JSON (strict schema) for downstream ETL + auditability for regulatory review.
- Security/ops: data residency in us-west, short retention window, and requirement for SOC2 evidence during procurement.

Proposed integration approach (high level)
1) Streaming generation + structured function-calling: use our streaming API to emit partial structured objects (JSON via function-calling) while the model continues to generate. This reduces perceived latency and allows early downstream validation.
2) Embedding-based rerank as a lightweight second-pass: generate N candidates, compute embeddings client-side (or via Redwood call), then run a fast rerank to pick the best answer. Keeps the heavy compute off the critical path for short queries.
3) SDK deltas: we’ll ship a small SDK patch that exposes: a streaming client with per-token hook, a function-calling wrapper returning validated JSON according to your schema, and an embeddings helper with batch and async options. See attached patch for API signatures.

Key tradeoffs we discussed
- KV/prefix caching is very helpful for repeated prompts but requires a warmup step for burst traffic — we recommend a short synthetic warmup during canary.
- Quantized model variant reduces cost but can slightly affect strict JSON formatting; we’ll include schema-enforced validation in the SDK to fail-fast.

Immediate asks for NovusAI
- Confirm max payload size (avg prompt length + typical context). Last time you mentioned ~1.2k tokens per request — please confirm.
- Confirm data residency and SOC2 contact for a short questionnaire.
- Sign off on pilot week (proposed window below).

Next steps / owners
- Hannah (AE): finalize SOW and push updated pilot MOP by 2027-06-24. (attachment: pilot-mop.xlsx)
- Connor (SE): prototype SDK delta (streaming + func-call) and demo by 2027-06-28.
- Ben (Eng): provide recommended model variant and initial latency SLO targets by 2027-06-25.

Proposed pilot window
- Canaries begin: week of 2027-07-05
- 2-week pilot: 2027-07-05 -> 2027-07-19

Attachments: redwood-postcall-deck-20270621.pdf, sdk-proposal-diff.patch, pilot-mop.xlsx

Looking forward — I’ll queue the SOW doc and calendar invites after Samir confirms payload size and SOC2 contact.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt

On Mon, Jun 21, 2027 at 2:03 PM Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Samir / Novus team — thanks again for your time today. Quick written recap + concrete next steps so we have alignment before the pilot kickoff.

Thanks Hannah — that all looks right. A few quick notes:
- Confirmed: average payload ~1.2k tokens, 95th percentile ~2.4k. We’ll send a small export (anonymized) by EOD Wed (incl. extremes).
- SOC2 contact: Priya Rao, priya.rao@novusai.com — she’ll take the questionnaire and coordinate.
- Pilot window works for us, prefer to start canary on 2027-07-06 (Tue) if that helps with our internal sched.

One ask: can your SDK provide an optional mode that enforces strict JSON output and returns an error code + sanitized fallback if the model does not conform? That would simplify our ETL pipeline and reduce engineering risk.

Samir
Head of Platform | NovusAI
samir@novusai.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 11:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call checkpoints — inference integration & SDK deltas (technical clarifications)

Hannah / team — quick technical notes to make sure the pilot runs smoothly:
- Model variant: start with the quantized 8-bit variant we validated in Q2 for similar doc-QA workloads; it gives ~2.3x throughput with minimal dev drift.
- JSON enforcement: implement a two-stage validator in the SDK — (1) schema validate during streaming (incremental checks), (2) post-generation strict parse. On failure, return an explicit error object with a short sanitized text fallback and a confidence score. This matches Samir's ask.
- KV cache warmup: recommend 500 synthetic warmup requests during canary for the most active routes. We’ll provide a script.
- Rerank latency: do candidate generation (N=6), then run embeddings-based rerank asynchronously with a 150ms budget for the reranker to keep overall 95th latency under 120ms for short queries. If rerank misses the deadline, return the top streaming candidate.

I’ll attach the warmup script and the model selection notes in a follow-up to engineering thread.

— Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
